Dear Sir or Madam,

We offer a price of €370.96 per unit, Zahlungsziel 30 days net, no Preisgleitklausel. 

Regarding our cost structure, CU-NOTATION rose 47.7 % in twelve months and is 20 % of our cost. Furthermore, LCI-C rose 2.7 % in twelve months and is 20 % of our cost. Additionally, PPI-C241 rose 6.5 % in twelve months and is 14 % of our cost.

Please note that this offer remains valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Petra Lechner
Key Account Manager, Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

move.subject: Re: Quote from Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG: Nordmark passes on copper for the 7.5 kW motor
move.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,

Thank you for your offer and for explaining your position.
Thank you for your letter and for the reliable supply of the motor over many years. We accept that copper has risen sharply and is a real cost driver for this motor, and we do not dispute it. We would like to reach a balanced result that your committee can approve quickly, recognising the cost movement in proportion. We therefore propose a moderate adjustment and, as an alternative, a copper-linked clause on a lower base.

Our data shows a different picture on some points:
Our demand forecast for this part has risen 11.9% (fc:350011@2026-09).
Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 348.32 per unit (po:4500014474-10, po:4500014413-10, po:4500014350-20).
Our recent quality notifications on this part average 4632 ppm (qn:20004826, qn:20004698).

Please find our proposal below.

We look forward to your reply.

Kind regards
Purchasing
Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH

move.text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

We have reviewed your offer and can adjust our Angebot as follows.

We checked the quality record data and price history data you cited; both hold, but they do not change our calculation. We also checked the volume change data you cited; it holds and we took it into account. Our technical department will review the quality notifications you referenced to ensure our high standards are met.

Our offer is a price of €373.88 per unit, Zahlungsziel 90 days net, no Preisgleitklausel. To support this price reduction, we must maintain our standard payment terms of 30 days net rather than the 90 days requested. Alternatively, with standard terms of Zahlungsziel 30 days net, we offer a price of €369.76 per unit, no Preisgleitklausel. 

A binding higher volume would help us and can improve the price. Which volume can you commit to? 

This offer is valid for 30 days.

Mit freundlichen Grüßen
Petra Lechner
Key Account Manager, Antriebstechnik Nordmark AG

key_points: Sole source on the motor; the fallback (Saalach) is far dearer at about twenty-one percent above today's price, so walking away is very costly. Stabilise goal plus the margin charge argue against squeezing.
Copper is a genuine cost driver. Accept it openly and never dispute the copper index.
Never cite should-cost (it shows the price below its cost), the rival quote or the notice period: they all favour Nordmark.
Main levers: the negotiation pattern (it settles well below its asks), flat order history, the rising forecast volume and the quality notifications on this part.
Negotiable terms are only price, payment days and the index clause; length, volume and effective date are fixed. Trades must therefore come from payment and the copper clause.

Copper is expected to rise about five percent. A zero-deadband clause on a twenty percent share adds roughly one percent of expected cost plus clause risk, so a clause is only worth it at a clearly lower base price.
Nordmark is not cash-stressed, so faster payment has modest value. Keep our standard sixty days and offer faster payment only as a closing sweetener if interest stays below the price gained.
The committee approves in fortnightly cycles. Keep sheets simple, answer promptly and accept a declared final offer.
plan.stance_why: Strategic sole-source part, price likely below its cost, fallback far dearer and a margin charge applies. Open moderately below the ask, with terms, rather than deep.

levers.why: Its own history shows settlements well below its asks, which anchors expectations for the committee.

argument.note: 3 renewals: asked +2.6% on average, settled -0.0% (gap 2.6 pp); last 2025-11-12: asked +4.7%, settled +1.2%. It usually settles well below its ask.

levers.why: Checkable forecast growth is a volume it values.

argument.sentence: Our demand forecast for this part has risen 11.9% (fc:350011@2026-09).
argument.note: Snapshot 2026-09: 6110 for the next 12 months against 5460 ordered in the last 12 months (requested dates); shared with suppliers: True. More volume is worth more to it.

levers.why: Checkable proof that today's price is the stable anchor.

argument.sentence: Our latest orders for this part were all at EUR 348.32 per unit (po:4500014474-10, po:4500014413-10, po:4500014350-20).
argument.note: What we pay now: [348.32, 348.32, 348.32] per unit (2026-08-31 to 2026-09-30); anchors any increase.

levers.why: Fresh, checkable quality issue on this part; supports a moderate step without a threat.

argument.sentence: Our recent quality notifications on this part average 4632 ppm (qn:20004826, qn:20004698).
argument.note: 2 supplier-caused complaints on this part in the last 12 months (leakage at test, wrong material certificate); EUR 300 recharged; 0 without a closed 8D. Per-lot ppm is jumpy (KNOWN_ISSUES 10): the scorecard's rolling ppm is the fairer figure.

levers.why: On-time delivery below target; a fresh-fact filler for a later round.

argument.sentence: Your rolling scorecard shows on-time delivery of 90.4% (sc:70510@2026Q3).
argument.note: Rolling 12 months to 2026-09-30: 90.4% on time against the requested date (90.4% against its own confirmed date); target 95%; peers' median 84.6%; class A green. A year earlier 84.0%.

levers.why: Shows we are a reliable payer and a fair customer.

argument.note: 149 invoices; we pay 1.1 days after due on average (last 12 months), 62.2% late, 0.0% over 10 days late, max 5; discounts taken 0 (0 after the period); short-paid 0. We pay reliably: a fair customer.

levers.why: Prices are fixed per calendar year until both sides agree, should it treat the increase as settled.

argument.sentence: Our framework agreement fixes prices for each calendar year.
argument.note: ctr:4600070510#3.1 (price): Prices as per the price annex, fixed for each calendar year. Changes require written notice of at least 90 days before the end of the calendar year.

trades.why: A copper clause with no deadband addresses its real pain. Offer it in an alternative sheet at a clearly lower base price, so the expected copper rise is priced in.
Our standard sixty days is already the contract norm, so keeping it costs Nordmark nothing new.
A minor sweetener for the last step, given only if the price gained exceeds the interest cost.

sup:70510.opening_paragraph: Thank you for your letter and for the reliable supply of the motor over many years. We accept that copper has risen sharply and is a real cost driver for this motor, and we do not dispute it. We would like to reach a balanced result that your committee can approve quickly, recognising the cost movement in proportion. We therefore propose a moderate adjustment and, as an alternative, a copper-linked clause on a lower base.
watch_for: Delays tied to committee cycles: answer promptly and do not push deadlines.
Wording such as 'final offer' or 'letztes Angebot': accept it, or take its cheaper alternative sheet.
Whether it prefers the clause sheet; check it is priced well below the fixed sheet.
Requests for faster payment or binding volume: volume is already fixed at our need, so restate it as binding.
Any claim about electronic component costs: weak for these motors, but do not ask about its cost structure.
How it prices payment days in its counter sheets.

risks: Squeezing too hard could provoke a walk-away; the fallback is far dearer and the margin charge applies.
A copper clause priced too generously raises our cost while copper keeps rising.
Slow committee cycles could look like a stall; letting rounds lapse hardens offers.
Evidence on personalities is thin, so the tone choice is uncertain.
Our should-cost estimate carries about five percent error, so its true floor is uncertain.
